focus: A10 plugin dependencies and tool definitions on both versions: what must .opencode/package.json and the plugin sources depend on so one plugin tree works on v1 and v2 without broken imports?

graphEvents.label: What dependency set and tool definition shape works on both hosts?
v1 tool() is an identity function; import buys only types and a zod re-export
plugin@1.18.34 already ships the v2 define/Plugin/PluginDomain surface
1.18.34 PluginContext has no tool, session, shell or tui domain
zod is an undeclared phantom dependency of the plugin tree
z.toJSONSchema in zod 4.1.8 bridges one shape to both hosts

label: v1's tool() is an identity function (`return input`, `tool.schema = z`), so the @opencode-ai/plugin/tool import contributes only types and a zod re-export; a tool definition can be declared as a plain {description,args,execute} object with zero behavioural change on v1. Confirmed by executing the helper: returned keys are exactly description,args,execute.

v1 tool `args` is a zod raw shape (z.ZodRawShape) and execute receives z.infer<z.ZodObject<Args>>, so a v1 tool cannot be declared with a plain JSON Schema; the three repo call sites use tool.schema.enum/string/boolean accordingly.

@opencode-ai/plugin@1.18.34 already ships the v2 plugin surface at the ./v2/promise subpath (define, Plugin{id,setup}, PluginDomain{add,remove}), so ONE pinned version satisfies both the v1 tool import and the v2 plugin contract; no second dependency is needed for the dual default export that loads on both hosts.

1.18.34's PluginContext declares only nine domains (options, agent, aisdk, catalog, command, integration, plugin, reference, skill) — no tool, session, shell or tui — and dist/v2/promise has no tool.* file, so ctx.tool.transform(...) is a 2.0.x-only API and cannot come from the version we ship.

The Reload mixin exists in the 1.18.34 v2 surface (declared in registration.d.ts, applied to agent/catalog/command/integration/reference/skill but not to plugin or aisdk), retiring the iteration-2 P2 concern for the shipped package; 2.0.32 parity remains unverified.

zod 4.1.8 is a phantom dependency: .opencode/package.json declares only @opencode-ai/plugin, and zod resolves solely because that package depends on it and npm hoists, so every tool.schema.* call in the three plugins rests on an undeclared transitive dependency that fails at module load if the plugin pin moves or the install layout stops hoisting.

One zod raw shape can feed both hosts: z.toJSONSchema(z.object(shape), {io:'input'}) exists in zod 4.1.8 and emitted draft 2020-12 output, so the v1 raw-shape vs v2 JSON-Schema divergence is bridgeable from one source of truth with a two-line adapter rather than one literal object per host.

The 2.0.32 half of A10 is unverifiable in this workspace: scratch/ does not exist at the repo root, so scratch/a2-v2pkg/... and scratch/cli-help/v2-plugin-help.txt named by the focus could not be re-read, and no unpacked 2.0.x copy was found; every 2.0.32 claim stays carried, and F4 is a downgrade signal since the 1.18.34 surface is strictly smaller than the described 2.0.32 surface.

Recommended dependency set is {@opencode-ai/plugin: 1.18.34, zod: 4.1.8} with the @opencode-ai/plugin/tool import dropped in favour of a local identity helper plus a direct zod import, because v1 auto-installs .opencode/package.json deps and therefore resolves whatever version is pinned — so a 2.x pin would put a 2.0.x copy on the v1 side and any subpath it stops exporting (./tool) becomes a load-time crash.
No plugin may import a package whose resolution differs between hosts; any bare specifier in .opencode/plugins is a potential load-time failure on a host that does not install .opencode/package.json.
Every runtime dependency a plugin imports must be declared in .opencode/package.json, never inherited through npm hoisting of a transitive dependency.

direction: Declare the tool `args` as a plain JSON Schema and rely on v1 accepting it
reason: v1's declared contract is z.ZodRawShape with execute typing from z.infer<z.ZodObject<Args>>; the identity wrapper does not validate, so the host does.

direction: Add @opencode-ai/plugin@2.0.32 alongside 1.18.34 to get ctx.tool on v2
reason: v1 auto-installs .opencode/package.json, so the pinned copy is what v1 resolves; a 2.x pin in that file is a v1-side dependency, and 2.0.32 is ESM-only with exact-pinned siblings and an unverified ./tool export.

direction: Keep the existing import and guard it with a dynamic-import fallback
reason: The import is inert on v1 (identity function), so removing it entirely is strictly simpler and immune to the ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED class, which a fallback only survives at the cost of an extra async load path per plugin.
